text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?

## Abstract

GSE309890 is a Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) Series retrieved via the `geo_series` tool, describing an RNA-seq expression profiling study of *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 (platform GPL24659, BioProject PRJNA1363958). The study investigates how the antidepressant sertraline biases antibiotic resistance evolution through stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway, implicating the transketolase A (tktA) gene in a reversible, mutation-agnostic metabolic mechanism of resistance. The Series contains 6 samples: 3 replicates each of untreated controls and cells subjected to 40-day adaptive evolution. No PubMed record is currently linked to this Series, indicating it is unpublished or not yet indexed. Querying the record's FTP directory returned exactly one supplementary file, `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz` (510 KB, last modified 2025-11-14), containing FPKM expression values for all 6 samples. GEO's metadata API does not itself serve processed expression values; only this compressed CSV file, hosted on the NCBI GEO FTP tree, provides that data. This result establishes precisely what is downloadable from this Series and clarifies that no other file formats (e.g., raw counts, BAM, or per-sample files) are currently deposited.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** GEO Series are curated collections of functional genomics experiments; GSE309890 profiles gene expression in *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 under an antidepressant-exposure adaptive evolution paradigm, relevant to the growing concern that selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) may inadvertently promote antibiotic resistance in bacteria colonizing SSRI users.

**Literature Review.** The `geo_series` tool call returned `pubmed_ids: []` with the note: "No PubMed record is linked to this GEO record... typically an unpublished or not-yet-indexed study." No literature was retrieved for this query.

**Knowledge Gap.** Prior to this query, it was unknown (a) what biological question this specific Series addresses, and (b) which concrete files are available for download versus which data types (e.g., raw counts) are absent from the deposit.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The objective was to determine the study description and enumerate the actual downloadable supplementary files for GSE309890. No statistical hypothesis applies; this is a descriptive metadata retrieval task.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** A single targeted metadata query was routed to NCBI GEO because the question names a specific GSE accession, for which GEO is the canonical source of both study description and the FTP-hosted supplementary file listing.

**Materials.** NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), queried through the `geo_series` tool.

**Procedures.** One tool call: `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true)`. This call retrieves the Series summary record via NCBI's esummary API (db=gds, id=200309890) and separately lists the record's FTP supplementary directory.

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistics were computed. The sample count (6) and file count (1) are direct counts from the tool's returned JSON fields (`sample_count` and the length of `supplementary_files`), not derived or filtered further.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

Table 1. GSE309890 study metadata

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Accession | GSE309890 |
| Organism | *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing |
| Platform | GPL24659 |
| Sample count | 6 |
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 |
| Linked PubMed IDs | None |
| Public date | 2026/02/01 |

Table 2. Samples in GSE309890

| Accession | Title |
|---|---|
| GSM9284457 | E. coli, control, rep1 |
| GSM9284458 | E. coli, control, rep2 |
| GSM9284459 | E. coli, control, rep3 |
| GSM9284460 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep1 |
| GSM9284461 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep2 |
| GSM9284462 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep3 |

Table 3. Downloadable supplementary file(s)

| File name | Size | Last modified | URL |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | 510K | 2025-11-14 11:10 | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz |

**Findings.** GSE309890 comprises 6 samples (3 control, 3 forty-day adaptive-evolution replicates). Exactly 1 supplementary file is listed under the Series' FTP suppl directory: `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz`, a gzip-compressed CSV of FPKM values across all 6 samples, 510 KB in size. The tool's `supplementary_file_types` field reports "CSV" as the only file type present. No raw count matrices, BAM/FASTQ files, or per-sample supplementary files are listed at the Series level.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The Series metadata directly answers what the study is about: it examines how sertraline exposure biases the evolutionary trajectory of antibiotic resistance in *E. coli* through rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway, with tktA implicated as a reversibility switch. For downloads, the only processed data product deposited at the Series level is the single FPKM CSV file.

**Context.** No PubMed-linked literature exists yet for this Series, so no external retrieved records support or extend this description beyond the GEO metadata itself.

**Limitations.** The tool's own provenance note states: "GEO's API returns metadata only. The processed expression values... are not available from any E-utilities call. They exist only inside the files listed under supplementary_files." Additionally, raw sequencing reads (FASTQ/SRA) are not part of this file listing; those would reside under the linked BioProject (PRJNA1363958) via SRA, which was not queried here. The unpublished status (no PubMed link) means no peer-reviewed contextualization is available.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 is about sertraline-driven metabolic rewiring underlying antibiotic resistance evolution in *E. coli*, and the only directly downloadable processed file is the FPKM CSV covering all 6 samples. A useful next query would be to resolve BioProject PRJNA1363958 via `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project` to identify and download the underlying raw sequencing runs (FASTQ files) for reanalysis.

## References

[1] NCBI GEO, GSE309890 record: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO FTP, Series directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[3] NCBI GEO FTP, supplementary files directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
[4] NCBI GEO FTP, downloadable file: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz

## Acknowledgments

Data provider: NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), including its underlying esummary/E-utilities API and public FTP archive.
